newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian farmers say A$ fall to boost investment.
newsitem.headline: Australian farmers say A$ fall to boost investment.

text.p: The recent decline in the alue of the Australian dollar would mean a windfall for the Australian economy which could boost investment in agricultural plant and equipment, Beverley Jordan, economist with the New South Wales Farmers' Association, said on Thursday.

"A lower dollar should not be seen as totally bad news," Jordan said in a statement. "For exporters who drive much of the activity in the Australian market, it means increased cash earnings in the period of the change," she said.

Every one cent fall in the value of the local dollar against the U.S. dollar meant increased earnings of about A$356 million for Australian farmers, Jordan said. She said the lower exchange rate could help increase business confidence in regional centres and major manufacturing cities around Australia.
Exchange rates had a big impact on Australian farm incomes because the majority of farm produce is exported and less than a third of its inputs are imported, the economist said.
The danger in a continuing fall in the value of the local dollar was that increased costs of imports would translate into increases in inflation, she said.
"The current outlook, with reasonably strong international demand for commodities, suggests that risk is low," Jordan said.
"At a time when farm margins are forecast to continue their declining trend in the short-term, an increase in our terms of trade is just what some farmers need," she said.
